newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Campaigning for the March 21 local government election ends at midnight today.
Government announces setting up of human rights commission with wide monitoring and investigative powers.
Prime Minister Sirima Bandaranaike appeals for a violence-free election. Over 1,000 incidents of election-related violence have been reported so far.
Sri Lanka air force grounds it last remaining Pucara light ground attack aircraft after one crashed on the weekend.
About 5,000 schools being used as polling stations in Friday's election will be closed on Thursday and Friday.
Air force investigating if Saturday's crash of Pucara aircraft was due to missile attack by separatist Tamil rebels.

More than 1,500 election-related violent incidents reported to police. Of this, 656 complaints made by main opposition United National Party activists and 597 made by supporters of the ruling People's Alliance coalition.
Foreign minister Lakshman Kadirgamar on three-day official visit to Pakistan, his first since that country's new government came to power.
Police say they will arrest anyone believed to be engaging in illegal acts, such as ballot stuffing, during Friday's election and hold them without bail for two weeks.
